sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Mr. Devid .J who met with road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of the petitioners case is as under:
That on 09-04-2022 at about 9-00 am., Sri.Devid J was standing in footpath on the left side of the road and when he reached Doddakammanahalli lake, Nice road,
Bangalore, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-35-EA-0917 came from Electronic city in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to Devid J and vehicle, ran over the head of Devid J, result of which Devid J sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately Devid J was shifted to Kavery Hospital wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to St.John's Medical College Hospital.
3. Prior to the accident, Mr.Devid J was doing agriculture work cum Milk vending and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

Due to the death of Devid J, the petitioner has suffered mental shock,
agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 / the R.C. owner of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 35-EA-0917 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. The respondent No.2- the Insurer of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-35-EA-0917 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that, it is after lapse of 10 months 14 days from the date of alleged accident, the deceased breathed his lost and the petitioner filed claim petition on 8-6-2023 ie., after one year 4 months from the date of accident that too after the death of her husband and that no medical records has been produced by the claimant to substantiate that the death of the deceased was due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
The respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the nexus between the death and the injuries sustained in the accident.
Hence, submitted to dismiss the claim petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that Sri Devid J died on account of the road traffic accident occurred on 09-04-2022 at about 09-00 am., near Doddakammanahalli lake, Nice road, Bangalore city, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Igneshamma vs Manjunath on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173775842/
2 motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 35-EA-0917?
2.
Whether the petitioner proves that she is entitled to the compensation amount claimed?
If so from whom and to what extent?

3. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and two witnesses are examined as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P23.

On the other hand, Fr.
Shanth Kumar J - Parish Priest was examined as RW.1 and Burrial certificate with Form No.4-A is marked as Ex.R1.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3:
As per final order for the Following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is the specific case of the petitioner that she is the legal heir of Devid .J.
(hereinafter called the deceased) who died in the Road Traffic Accident on account of the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-35-EA-0917 (hereinafter called the offending vehicle).
To this effect the petitioner has filed her affidavit in lieu of oral evidence and in support of her contention; she has relied upon documentary evidence at Ex.P.1 to 8 which are the police records.

She has produced the medical documents marked as Ex.P9 to Ex.P16.
11.

The documents above referred makes out that, on the basis of the complaint lodged by the petitioner/Smt.Igneshamma, case was registered against the rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 338 IPC 12.
If the materials placed on record is perused, the accident in question was occurred on 09-04-2022 at 9-00 a.m.
Complaint came to be lodged on the same date at 12-00 pm.
The complaint is lodged by the petitioner who is an eye witness to the accident.
In the complaint the vehicle number involved in the accident is mentioned so also the name of the rider of the said vehicle.

In the claim petition it is stated that at the time of accident the deceased was standing in the footpath and offending vehicle which came from Electronic City in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the deceased who was standing in the footpath.
But if the complaint is perused, wherein it is stated that at the time of accident the deceased was crossing the road and the offending vehicle which came from Electronic city hit to the deceased.

If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, it is Igneshamma vs Manjunath on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173775842/
3 a double road of the width of 40 feet each and the accident in question has occurred in the middle of the road leads from Electronic City towards Bannerghatta road.

sentences.text: Hence from the scene of occurrence it can be gathered that the deceased while crossing the road met with an accident.
Hence, the deceased being the pedestrian while stepping into the road and while crossing the road ought to have taken every care and caution by observing the vehicle moving in the said road.
Hence, it can be said that the deceased has also contributed negligence.
The rider of the offending vehicle was proceeding from Electronic City towards Bannerghatta road.
As per the sketch it is a straight road.

When deceased had already stepped in to the road and crossed all most half of the road, under such circumstances if the rider of the offending vehicle had ridden his motorcycle in a normal speed, on seeing the deceased crossing the road he could have avoided the accident by applying break or by taking his vehicle on the left side of the road.
When offending vehicle is a two wheeler, the rider ought to have ride his vehicle on the left side of the vehicle.
Hence, the topography of the scene of occurrence clearly discloses that the rider of the offending vehicle has contributed higher percentage of negligence.

Hence, by attributing 20% of negligence on the deceased and 80% on the rider of the motorcycle, it is ordered that the petitioner has to forgo compensation to the extent of 20% of negligence contributed by her husband.

13. It is not in dispute that though the deceased had sustained grievous injuries and incurred huge medical expenses but for the reason best known to the deceased, during his life time he had not filed claim petition for the injuries sustained by him.

It is after lapse of nearly 1 years from the date o accident the present application came to be filed by the petitioner claiming compensation for the death of her husband due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
14. It is relevant to state here that petitioner has filed IA No.I, u/Sec. 5 of the Limitation Act to condone the delay of 210 days in filing the claim petition.
For the said application the respondent no.2 who is the contesting respondent has not filed objection.
By oversight without considering the IA No.1, this court has proceeded with the case.
It is relevant to state here that regarding the accident in question, AIR Misc.,No. 580/2022 was filed and it was disposed off.

In the IA No.1 the petitioner has assigned reason stating that her husband had sustained grievous injuries and he was under treatment for quite long time hence it could not possible to file the claim petition in time.
15. If the materials placed on record is perused, the deceased had sustained head injury and other injuries and for quite long time he had taken treatment and he was bed ridden for a quite long time.

16. In the judgment rendered by Writ Petition No.201931/2023 between The Divisional Manger,
United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Ramu @ Ramesh & Ors., it was observed by the Hon'ble High Court that Sec.166 of the MV Act provides for a claim of compensation to be made on account of either injury or death being caused due to a motor vehicle accident.

sentences.text: It is amply clear that section 166 of the MV Act is a beneficial provision which is contained in the MV Act as amended from time to time to provide benefit to any injured or to the legal representatives of the deceased.
The object of section 166 of the MV Act being beneficial, any provision to be applied relating thereto would also be required to be applied beneficially".
Hence, delay of 210 days can be condoned,

By considering the fact that soon after the accident AIR Mis case was registered and by considering the observation made in the aforesaid ruling, there is every reason to condone the delay in filing the petition.

As observed supra, the respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the nexus between the death and injuries sustained by the deceased and submitted that no postmortem was conducted hence cause of death is not proved and that petitioner has not given further complaint regarding the death of her husband due to the accidental injuries and no additional charge sheet has been filed invoking Sec.

18.

Per contra it is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for petitioner that because of the grievous head injuries and other injuries sustained by the deceased he was bed ridden till his death and the injuries sustained in the accident is the direct cause for the death.
So far as the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 regarding not conducted postmortem is concerned
, it is submitted by the learned counsel for petitioner that merely because the postmortem was not conducted it cannot be said that the death was not due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

The learned counsel at this juncture has referred the judgment reported in MFA No.
10285/2013 between Smt. Gowramma & Ors.,Vs.
M / S United
Indian
Insurance Co.Ltd., & Anr.,
decided on 15-10-2024.
In the said case, the injured sustained grievous injuries to the head and other parts of the body.
The injuries caused had effected severely to his neurological system and after one year and two months of the accident he died.
The claim petition was filed by the deceased when he was alive but during the pendency of the claim petition he died.

The claim petition filed by the deceased seeking compensation on account of injuries sustained by him was dismissed by the Tribunal on the ground that after the death of deceased postmortem was not conducted and other medical evidence on record do not prove the nexus between the injuries sustained in the accident and the death of the deceased.
In the said case, treated doctor has given clear evidence that there is nexus between the injuries sustained and cause of death.
Under the given set of fact the Hon'ble High Court has raised point whether considering the time gap between accident and death occurred is having direct nexus to the injuries sustained.

By considering the evidence of medical expert and the nature of injuries sustained by the deceased, it was observed that "conducting postmortem cannot be expected where the time gap between the accidental injuries and death occurred is ranging for several months.
Therefore, just because, postmortem is not conducted is not a ground to reject the other medical evidence including the expert evidence.

Though, in the absence of postmortem report, the other medical records prove the cause of death of the deceased due to neurological complications occurred in the brain of the deceased developing uncontrolled epilepsy"
and accordingly held that there is nexus between death and injuries sustained by the deceased.

19. In MFA No. 20156/2013 (MV) between United Indian Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Smt. Dundavva &
Anr., decided on 11-02-2013.

In the light of the argument canvassed by the learned respective counsels and the observation made in the aforesaid judgment, if the evidence of PW.1 and PW.3 is read, the PW.1 has admitted that there is no medical document to prove that death of deceased was due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

PW.3 - the Medical Officer St John's Medical Hospital has deposed that, at the time when deceased was admitted in their hospital, the injuries mentioned in the discharge summaries are found in the body of the deceased and there is possibility of person death due to the said injuries and that since deceased was aged about 67 years even if surgery was conducted there was no possibility of his recover hence surgery was not conducted.

According to the PW.3 the deceased has sustained grievous head injuries and since there is respiratory problem, pipe was fixed and that because of heavy medical expenses, against to the medical advice, the deceased was discharged and after the discharge the deceased had not taken follow up treatment.

At the time of discharge against to the medical advice, it was made it clear to the deceased and his family members about the difficulty in taking treatment at home and that nursing care is required and there may be possibility of getting the wound infected.

It is deposed by PW.3 that after the discharge, deceased was bed ridden and on 06-06-2022 the deceased visited the hospital, by that time his sugar level was 400 and he was suffering from fever and there was bed sore and though he was advised to admit in the hospital as an inpatient but he has taken treatment in OPD and thereafter the deceased did not come for follow up treatment at any time .

It is deposed by Pw.3 that had the deceased taken follow up treatment the possibility of his death at that event was very less and that since deceased did not come to their hospital after 06-06-2022, he has no knowledge / information about the cause for death.

From the evidence of PW.3 and from the medical documents it can be gathered that from 10-04-2022 to 14-05-2022 the deceased was admitted as an inpatient at St. John's Hospital and till 02-05-2022 he was in the ICU and on 14-05-2022 also against to the medical advice he got discharged from the hospital.

It is deposed by PW.3 that since deceased had sustained grievous injuries and he was in the hospital for quite long period, and after the discharge deceased was bed ridden and had bed sore and suffered from pneumonia, urine infection etc., it can be said that death of deceased was due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
It is further deposed by PW.3 that since deceased had not taken follow up treatment and since postmortem was not conducted, he is not in a position to state the cause for death.

21. Though the PW.3 at one breath has deposed that the injuries sustained by the deceased in the accident may be the cause for death but he has categorically deposed that, if the deceased who is diabetic patient had taken proper follow up treatment, there was no possibility of his succumbed to the injuries.
Hence, from the evidence of PW.3, the court cannot assess the cause of death.

sentences.text: As observed supra, the deceased was a diabetic patient and against to the medical advice he got discharged from the hospital.
Even after discharge he has not taken follow up treatment till his death.
Hence, there is clear negligence on the part of the deceased in not taking proper treatment.
Further if the evidence of RW.1 is perused, RW.1 is a parish priest and the church in which RW.1 was the priest, the dead body of the deceased was buried.
The respondent no.2 has marked the burrial certificate through RW.1 as Ex.R1 wherein the cause of death is mentioned as "due to Chronic Bronchite of old age and Cardio Respiratory Arrest".

Hence, it can be said that deceased was died not due to the accidental injuries but for other injuries and there is no supportive evidence to prove the direct nexus between the death and injuries sustained in the accident.
But it can be gathered that the deceased had met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries.

Hence, by assessing the negligence contributed by the deceased at 20% and the rider of the offending vehicle at 80%, it is ordered that the petitioner being the legal representatives of the deceased has to forgo compensation to an extent of 20% out of the total compensation.
Hence, I answer issue no.1 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue no 2 :
The petitioner is the wife of the deceased.
The petitioner filed petition claiming compensation for the death caused due to the accidental injuries.

But this court after going through the records arrived at firm conclusion that death of the deceased was not due to the accidental injury sustained by him but due to Cardiac Arrest and other age related problems and also due to the clear negligence on the part of deceased.

Now the question to be decided is under what are all the heads,
the petitioner being the legal heir of deceased is entitled to get compensation.
24.

It is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for petitioner that in the event if court comes to the conclusion that deceased was not died due to the injuries sustained in the accident then his legal heir is entitled for compensation for loss of estate which includes expenditure on medicines,
treatment, diet, attendant, doctors fee etc including income and future prospects which would have caused reasonable accretion to the estate but for the sudden expenditure which had to be met from the depleted the estate of the injured.

The learned counsel at this juncture has referred observation made by the hon'ble Supreme court in Civil Appeal No. 4800/2021 (arising out of SLP (C)
No.2873/2021) between The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon (deceased) through his Legal Representative Narinder Kahlon Gosakan & Anr.,

In the said case,
original claimant was severely injured in a Motor Accident.
He filed claim petition.
During the pendency of the Appeal he was died.
The counsel for Insurance company made submission that the cause of action being personal to the injured abates on his death.
The legal heir is entitled only to such compensation which forms part of the estate of the deceased.

Loss of salary, future prospects,
pain and suffering long with attendant charges do not form part of the estate of the deceased.
The compensation could not have been fixed by application of multiplier as it was not a case of death caused or occasioned by or due to the accident.

25. It was held that "The Act is a beneficial and welfare legislation, Section 166(1) (a) of the Act provides for a statutory claim for compensation arising out of an accident by the person who has sustained the injury.
Under Clause (b), compensation is payable to the owner of the property.
In case of death, the legal representatives of the deceased can pursue the claim.
Property, under the Act, will have a much wider connotation than the conventional definition.
If the legal heirs can Igneshamma vs Manjunath on 3 October, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173775842/
7 pursue claims in case of death

, we see no reason why the legal representatives cannot purse claims for loss of property akin to estate of the injured if he is deceased subsequently for reasons other than attributable to the accident or injuries under Clause 1(c) of Section 166.
Such a claim would be completely distinct from personal injuries to the claimant and which may not be the cause of death.
Such claims of personal injuries would undoubtedly abate with the death of the injured.
What would the loss of estate mean and what items would be covered by it are issues which has to engage our attention.
The appellant has a statutory obligation to pay compensation in motor accident claim cases.

This obligation cannot be evaded behind the defence that it was available only for personal injuries and abates on his death irrespective of the loss caused to the estate of the deceased because of the injuries.

26. In Umedchand Golcha Vs. Dayaram & Ors., it was observed that "the claim for personal injuries will not survive on death of the injured unrelated to the accident but the legal representatives could pursue the claim for enhancement of the claim for loss of the estate which would include expenditure on medical expenses, traveling, attendant, diet, doctor's fee and reasonable monthly annual accretion to the estate for a certain period.
It is trite that the income which a person derives compositely forms part of the expenditure on himself, his family and the savings go to the estate.

The unforeseen expenses as aforesaid naturally have to be met from the estate causing pecuniary loss to the estate".
27.

Per contra the learned counsel for the respondent no 2 has submitted that when death is not due to the accidental injuries sustained by the deceased , the legal heir is entitled to claim compensation to the extent of loss of estate and not towards loss of dependency and other general damages.
Medical expenses and loss of income during treatment would constitute loss of estate.

28. If the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme court referred by the learned counsel for the petitioner is read in whole where in question was raised as to " if death of injured subsequently for reasons other than attributable to the accident injuries what would be the loss of estate mean and what items would be covered by it.

It was observed that claim for personal injuries will not survive on death of the injured unrelated to the accident but the legal representatives could pursue the claim for enhancement of the claim for loss of estate which would include expenditure on medical expenses, travelling attendant, diet, doctors fee including income and future prospects which would have caused reasonable accretion to the estate but for the sudden expenditure which had to be met from and depleted the estate of the injured subsequently deceased.
29.

Keeping in mind the observation made in the aforesaid judgment, coming to the case in hand,
the deceased had sustained bodily injuries as the impact of accident.

However the compensation under the head pain and sufferings being personal in nature held to be un sustainable and legal heir is not entitled to claim compensation for the injuries sustained by the deceased petitioner.

36. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,51,240/- (Rupees Six Lakh Fifty One Thousand Two Hundred Forty only).

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence from the scene of occurrence it can be gathered that the deceased while crossing the road met with an accident.
Hence, the deceased being the pedestrian while stepping into the road and while crossing the road ought to have taken every care and caution by observing the vehicle moving in the said road.
Hence, it can be said that the deceased has also contributed negligence.
When deceased had already stepped in to the road and crossed all most half of the road, under such circumstances if the rider of the offending vehicle had ridden his motorcycle in a normal speed, on seeing the deceased crossing the road he could have avoided the accident by applying break or by taking his vehicle on the left side of the road.
When offending vehicle is a two wheeler, the rider ought to have ride his vehicle on the left side of the vehicle.
Hence, the topography of the scene of occurrence clearly discloses that the rider of the offending vehicle has contributed higher percentage of negligence.
Hence, by attributing 20% of negligence on the deceased and 80% on the rider of the motorcycle, it is ordered that the petitioner has to forgo compensation to the extent of 20% of negligence contributed by her husband.
It is after lapse of nearly 1 years from the date o accident the present application came to be filed by the petitioner claiming compensation for the death of her husband due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
The injuries caused had effected severely to his neurological system and after one year and two months of the accident he died.
The claim petition was filed by the deceased when he was alive but during the pendency of the claim petition he died.
The claim petition filed by the deceased seeking compensation on account of injuries sustained by him was dismissed by the Tribunal on the ground that after the death of deceased postmortem was not conducted and other medical evidence on record do not prove the nexus between the injuries sustained in the accident and the death of the deceased.
In the said case, treated doctor has given clear evidence that there is nexus between the injuries sustained and cause of death.
19. In MFA No. 20156/2013 (MV) between United Indian Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Smt. Dundavva &
Anr., decided on 11-02-2013.
21. Though the PW.3 at one breath has deposed that the injuries sustained by the deceased in the accident may be the cause for death but he has categorically deposed that, if the deceased who is diabetic patient had taken proper follow up treatment, there was no possibility of his succumbed to the injuries.
Hence, from the evidence of PW.3, the court cannot assess the cause of death.
Even after discharge he has not taken follow up treatment till his death.
Hence, there is clear negligence on the part of the deceased in not taking proper treatment.
Further if the evidence of RW.1 is perused, RW.1 is a parish priest and the church in which RW.1 was the priest, the dead body of the deceased was buried.
Hence, it can be said that deceased was died not due to the accidental injuries but for other injuries and there is no supportive evidence to prove the direct nexus between the death and injuries sustained in the accident.
Hence, by assessing the negligence contributed by the deceased at 20% and the rider of the offending vehicle at 80%, it is ordered that the petitioner being the legal representatives of the deceased has to forgo compensation to an extent of 20% out of the total compensation.
But this court after going through the records arrived at firm conclusion that death of the deceased was not due to the accidental injury sustained by him but due to Cardiac Arrest and other age related problems and also due to the clear negligence on the part of deceased.
Property, under the Act, will have a much wider connotation than the conventional definition.
, we see no reason why the legal representatives cannot purse claims for loss of property akin to estate of the injured if he is deceased subsequently for reasons other than attributable to the accident or injuries under Clause 1(c) of Section 166.
Such a claim would be completely distinct from personal injuries to the claimant and which may not be the cause of death.
Such claims of personal injuries would undoubtedly abate with the death of the injured.
The appellant has a statutory obligation to pay compensation in motor accident claim cases.
This obligation cannot be evaded behind the defence that it was available only for personal injuries and abates on his death irrespective of the loss caused to the estate of the deceased because of the injuries.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the deceased which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of eight months as complete laid down period.
